positive: Rename and re-export each standard control and operator declaration; run the same branch/effect/cleanup trace.
negative: A same-spelled unrelated declaration must not gain intrinsic control or arithmetic privileges.
boundary: Change module paths, import order and prefix/infix aliases independently; include a user-defined selector.
oracle: Compare resolved provider identities modulo the rename and the complete observable trace, not just the final integer.

positive: Distinct names and explicitly trait-qualified operations coexist with different signatures.
negative: Reject duplicate free or inherent member names with different arity, bounds, safety or parameter types.
boundary: Repeat through alias-qualified impls and two package re-export paths; identical provider imports deduplicate.
oracle: Source diagnostic identifies both declarations; no artifact is published for a real conflict.

positive: Assign and uniquely borrow a let-mut local; mutate through an immutable binding holding a unique reference.
negative: Reject reassignment or unique borrowing of an immutable owned local, and reassignment of the immutable reference binding.
boundary: Exercise projections, moved-out restoration and RHS side effects before replacement cleanup.
oracle: Acceptance and ordered event trace distinguish binding permission, referent permission and resident ownership.

positive: Call zero-, one-, two-argument and single-tuple-argument functions with matching Fn argument packs.
negative: Reject grouped T as an argument-tuple contract and mismatched (T,U) versus ((T,U),).
boundary: Unit, singleton tuple, nested singleton, tuple-pattern callable and effect payload arities all remain distinct.
oracle: Inspect selected Args and verify the callee receives the exact values in source order.

positive: Resolve one callable first, then infer a trailing contextual block from its selected Fn/RunsIn contract.
negative: Reject ambiguous contextual interpretation and a computed noncallable value passed where a callable is required.
boundary: Compare explicit fn, zero-argument compact form, unnamed duplicable arguments and an ordinary eager block.
oracle: Invocation log proves only callable bodies are deferred; diagnostics explain ambiguity rather than guessing from names.

positive: Construct, pass and store a callback with a visible body effect; invoke it later exactly once.
negative: A harness mutation that executes the body during construction or passing must fail the event assertion.
boundary: Capture initializers still execute at the argument position; a skipped affine callback cleans its captures without running its body.
oracle: Separate capture-formation, invocation, effect and destructor events in an exact trace.

positive: Match imported constructor aliases and structural Bool/None constants, including an explicit let binder shadowing a constant.
negative: Reject qualified unresolved constants and floating constant patterns; no effectful initializer or Eq call may implement matching.
boundary: Use a deliberately observable Eq implementation, nested constant aggregates and different alias paths.
oracle: No Eq/initializer event occurs; selected clause and normalized constructor identity match structural expectations.

positive: Explicit import beats prelude/glob candidates and a lexical local may shadow an import.
negative: Reject two distinct explicit candidates even when only one has type-compatible arguments.
boundary: Permute source/import order; two paths to the same provider are not an ambiguity.
oracle: Stable source diagnostics name both distinct candidates; resolution does not depend on expected type or handler proximity.

positive: Import an effect family, selectively alias an operation and pass that operation as a callable; all perform the same instance.
negative: Reject missing effect permission or host authority despite successful name import.
boundary: Family alias leaves operation names unchanged; re-exports and generic operation instances preserve identity.
oracle: Resolved operation IDs, exact outward rows and handler event traces agree without generated forwarding wrappers.

positive: Construct and project a tuple struct through permitted pub fields while preserving its nominal type.
negative: Reject tuple-to-tuple-struct substitution and private field construction/projection/deconstruction from a sibling module.
boundary: Declaring descendants retain authority across separate source files; parent, sibling and facade access are checked separately.
oracle: Layout/projection results and source privacy/type diagnostics use declaration/module identity, not file identity.

positive: Accept exhaustive ordered pattern callables that transfer every owned exact-linear field.
negative: Reject missing variants, unreachable clauses, duplicate binders and a wildcard/rest that discards a linear subtree.
boundary: Borrowed wildcard observation is distinct from owned disposal; include arrays, references and non-exhaustive foreign enums.
oracle: Exhaustiveness and disposal diagnostics are independently exercised using otherwise valid fixtures.

positive: One multi-clause callable consumes one common ticket on every normal branch.
negative: Reject a branch that consumes it twice or leaves it live at a normal exit.
boundary: Borrow disjoint places in different clauses and include a diverging branch without inventing simultaneous loans.
oracle: One capture owner and one selected invocation; owner ledger balances on every reachable path.

positive: Clause-local names resolve only in that clause; a bottom clause joins a differently typed normal result.
negative: Reject a sibling reference to another clause's binder or a fabricated normal post-state from a diverging clause.
boundary: Nested pattern callables reuse source spellings with distinct binder identities.
oracle: Binding identities, result type and terminal cleanup trace match lexical scope.

positive: Select one Result implementation through its Bool and Option aliases.
negative: Reject overlapping alias-qualified Eq/Default/Display or other impls, including different surface names for the same head.
boundary: Generic payload restrictions and associated projections normalize before the overlap decision.
oracle: Coherence diagnostic identifies equivalent normalized heads; no alias-specific implementation selection.

positive: Inline mutually exclusive conditional bodies each consume the same incoming ticket exactly once.
negative: Reject two independently materialized owning closures that capture that same ticket.
boundary: Store only after the linked island has sealed; user-defined selectors follow the same rule.
oracle: Owner inventory distinguishes one correlated incoming environment from two physical capture owners.

positive: Sequential callbacks are accepted when the second uses only the first callback's actual post-environment.
negative: Reject reuse of a resident consumed by the first callback, even if both callbacks have the same effect row.
boundary: Exercise zero, one and two executed callbacks through nested and/or composition.
oracle: Per-path invocation sequence and owner ledger; effect permissions never stand in for use counts.

positive: A callback mutates or consumes state and returns Err; recovery uses the resulting post-state.
negative: Reject recovery that reuses the pre-callback owner as though Err rolled back its consumption.
boundary: Distinguish a skipped Err path from an Err produced after invocation; nest both under aliases.
oracle: Guarded result provenance and event log retain effects and ownership changes already performed.

positive: Seal a conditional Result when all retained availability obligations admit lawful closure.
negative: Reject an unresolved Available witness escaping via a local, aggregate, return, opaque call or serialized interface.
boundary: A complete inline conditional is valid while splitting the identical source at an unsealable binding boundary is not.
oracle: Each escape form gets a source-oriented obligation diagnostic; no invisible persistent typestate in plain Result.

positive: Conditionally move an affine resident, then leave scope or restore it before a whole-owner use.
negative: Reject reading or moving a maybe-initialized owner before definite restoration.
boundary: Nested joins, early exits, field-level partial initialization and repeated restoration preserve masks.
oracle: Drop events occur only on initialized paths at the specified cleanup boundary, never early solely to equalize branches.

positive: Transfer or authorizedly deconstruct an exact-linear resident on every normal/local/nonlocal path.
negative: Reject its loss through wildcard, statement discard, helper identity result, return, optional cancellation or terminal cleanup.
boundary: Wrap it in Option, arrays, closures, error payloads and opaque pointer owners.
oracle: Unique logical owner survives each transfer; destruction is never credited as a positive use.

positive: Transfer a fieldless linear ticket and destroy N zero-sized affine residents with observable hooks.
negative: Reject discarding a zero-sized linear owner or erasing a resident hook merely because its byte size is zero.
boundary: Contrast [Linear;0], [ZstLinear;1] and [ZstDrop;N], including partial initialization and mixed-engine transfer.
oracle: Logical resident IDs and destructor counts, not allocated byte counts, establish accounting.

positive: Destroy nested affine owners with custom hooks: hook then reverse fields, newest locals first.
negative: Reject Drop for a positive-lower owner and hooks that perform effects, suspend, move fields or transfer to labels.
boundary: Partial initialization, transferred return payloads and a diverging hook preserve only the required executed cleanup prefix.
oracle: Exact destructor identity/order/count and release-domain trace; no claim that a diverging hook terminates.

positive: Move a whole custom-Drop owner or borrow its fields through an authorized API.
negative: Reject safe field moves and owned pattern deconstruction when the concrete selected Drop applies.
boundary: Conditional generic Drop selected versus unselected after associated-type normalization; private fields remain separately protected.
oracle: Selection-dependent source rejection before emission; an unselected hook must not falsely prohibit an otherwise legal move.

positive: Move out through a unique reference, restore the resident, then leave or suspend lawfully.
negative: Reject an open hole crossing a label break, terminal handler exit, loan end, opaque call or continuation capture.
boundary: Immediate abort/proven nontermination is not treated as an ordinary cleanup-bearing exit; nested reborrows are included.
oracle: Initialization and loan obligations explain rejection; no successful path exposes invalid borrowed storage.

positive: After the last actual use of a returned/stored reference carrier, permit a previously conflicting mutation.
negative: Reject mutation, movement or destruction while any possible returned-origin loan remains live.
boundary: Multiple input origins, nested carriers, branch joins, reborrows and Drop-observed fields.
oracle: Accepted/rejected pairs differ only in the last use; returned references identify original storage.

positive: Use fresh higher-ranked regions through nested GAT/callback contracts without leaking their scope.
negative: Reject forcing an outer inference variable to contain a newer rigid region, brand, const or row placeholder.
boundary: Nested binders with repeated source names, projected associated results and separately compiled interfaces.
oracle: Rigid placeholder/leak-check diagnostic rather than inferred static lifetime or guessed trait evidence.

positive: Use each fresh label/environment brand only with its own originating scope and contract.
negative: Reject substitution of structurally identical footprints or same-result labels from different binders.
boundary: Recursive activations, higher-ranked labels, aliases and equal-size erased layouts do not collapse identities.
oracle: Brand identity stays invariant through inference, specialization and metadata admission.

positive: Evaluate an is subject once; transport justified positive/negative binders into the selected contextual callback.
negative: Reject escaping or forging binders, moving a borrowed noncopy projection and mutation while a protecting loan remains live.
boundary: Conjunction/disjunction/not, nested closure capture and equal-spelled distinct binder identities.
oracle: Subject counter, selected hidden Args, original loan origins and pack-resident cleanup are all asserted.

positive: Union two distinct callback rows, normalize proven duplicate instances and subtract only fully handled instances.
negative: Reject a nonunique split of known effects among unknown tails, unresolved executable rows and tuple-as-union notation.
boundary: Associated row projections after the bar, repeated brands/types/consts, row order and proper subset permission.
oracle: Exact normalized callable row is retained; no equality forcing between independent callback rows.

positive: An unqualified generic operation selects the nearest explicit contextual instance of its already resolved family.
negative: Reject an inner payload mismatch, two explicit defaults or a helper with only forwarded permissions and no unique default.
boundary: Same-family nested rows, reordered union terms, explicit type arguments and label-indexed selection.
oracle: Handler trace names the exact selected instance; type mismatch never falls back to an outer compatible instance.

positive: Nested handlers route to the nearest exact normalized instance and forward unmatched payload patterns in source order.
negative: Reject an outward row falsely claiming full handling when an operation or payload alternative remains uncovered.
boundary: Identical payload types with distinct brands; deep resumption and clause-emitted operations execute under correct delimiters.
oracle: Exact dispatch/completion/effect event trace plus outward-row inspection; no completion arm on forwarding/cancel/leave.

positive: Use payload-only tail-resume abbreviation for optional/exact one-shot operations when one is permitted.
negative: Reject abbreviation for exact-two and reject terminal-operation arms with a phantom continuation.
boundary: Explicit n+1 continuation binder versus n payloads, including zero-payload operations.
oracle: Selected continuation quantity and arm result contract; exact-two requires two explicit logical invocations.

positive: Exact-once suspension retains a linear obligation and resumes it once; optional cancellation cleans only affine residents.
negative: Reject optional capture of a linear resident, dropping an exact continuation and alias-based double resumption.
boundary: Capture before/after partial moves, nested handlers and continuation transfer through an aggregate.
oracle: Capture/snapshot inventory and per-owner events distinguish cancellation from successful exact-once transfer.

positive: Exact finite replay snapshots only initialized duplicable residual fields and consumes original authority on the last invocation.
negative: Reject live unique loans, labels, nonduplicable residents or unreplayable handler dependencies in multi-shot capture.
boundary: Move one field before capture; alias remaining shared references; test quantities 2 and 3 without calling Clone.
oracle: Replay counts, absence of moved slots, preserved alias relationships and exact residual cleanup trace.

positive: A terminal operation protects its payload and cleans legally abandoned locals before entering its clause.
negative: Reject a terminal transfer that would discard a linear resident or leave a live borrowed owner invalid.
boundary: Nested handler-owned captures and a caller-owned borrowed closure survive when outside the abandoned ownership region.
oracle: Payload identity and cleanup-before-clause ordering; no phantom resumption or destruction of unrelated owners.

positive: A generic label helper fuses to one active lexical destination through several source functions at O0.
negative: Reject foreign, unavailable-body, opaque indirect and unsupported recursive label boundaries that cannot be fused.
boundary: Recursive named-function activations and nested same-result labels retain distinct dynamic destinations.
oracle: Direct destination/control proof plus exact cleanup trace; no dynamic-stack-search fallback or addressable label value.

positive: Accept compatible direct/indirect tail transfer after lawful argument protection, cleanup and loan ending.
negative: Reject following work, dead-local references, completion transformations, retained delimiters and unproved cross-ABI transfer.
boundary: Owning receiver, effectful callee/argument evaluation and destruction order at a tail site.
oracle: Diagnostic identifies the source obligation; checked transfer is mandatory at every configured optimization level.

positive: Run direct, mutual and library-loop tail cycles at geometric iteration counts with observable output checks.
negative: A deliberately ordinary-recursive control fixture must exceed the same live-frame/control-storage bound so instrumentation is meaningful.
boundary: Nested scopes, per-iteration affine drops and both interpreter/native optimization configurations.
oracle: Measure live frames, handler depth and retained control/continuation bytes after warmup; bounded by input-independent constant, not total allocations or stack RSS alone.

positive: Invoke unsafe functions/callables only inside explicit unsafe scopes while retaining ordinary type and ownership checking.
negative: Reject permission inherited into a deferred closure body, unsafe calls inside an unsafe fn without a block, and a safe Fn claim for unsafe code.
boundary: Unsafe trait/impl agreement, unsafe RunsIn, aliases and effectful versus unsafe-only functions.
oracle: Separate safety qualifier and effect row diagnostics; unsafe never forges lifetime, privacy or use evidence.

positive: Exercise lawful initialized raw moves, duplicable copies, overlap variants and checked allocation/layout arithmetic.
negative: Safe wrappers reject invalid ranges; available instrumentation diagnoses invalid initialization/provenance/alignment without claiming arbitrary unsafe UB is statically decidable.
boundary: Zero size, one-past, near-usize overflow, partial initialization, unaligned operations and allocation failure.
oracle: Logical initialized-resident model, allocation-domain ledger and instrumentation reports; run unsafe-invalid probes only in isolated instrumented processes.

positive: Admit authentic intrinsic/callable/host identities with exact contracts and provenance-preserving operations.
negative: Reject forged brands, availability/binding evidence, callable identities and host grants made from names, bytes, addresses or FFI values.
boundary: Corrupt one authenticated field at a time while retaining equal size/alignment; include raw-pointer integer round trips.
oracle: Source or admission rejection before side effects; trusted unsafe violations are not claimed to be universally detected by the compiler.

positive: Round-trip advertised C scalar/repr(C) values and synchronous/registered callbacks through an actual C shim.
negative: Reject non-C owners, unadapted effects/labels, retained unregistered callbacks and incompatible symbol/capability contracts.
boundary: Target-specific c_long/c_bool, transparent layout, release-domain matching and unregister/re-entry scenarios.
oracle: C-computed sizeof/alignof/offsetof and actual callback/result traces; hazardous unwinding probes isolated, never invoked as ordinary valid code.

positive: Call VM to native to bytecode-only specialization and back with borrowed/owned residents sharing actual backing addresses.
negative: Reject mismatched lifetime/drop/domain contracts and unsupported mixed-control paths before execution.
boundary: VM frame growth, callbacks, transitive generic Drop, zero-sized residents and mutation in both directions.
oracle: Identity/address, mutation, transfer and selected-destructor ledger plus zero boundary marshalling allocations; separate runs with equal values are insufficient.

positive: Compile and execute target-sized usize/isize layouts and arithmetic under each declared target contract.
negative: Reject incompatible pointer width, endianness, layout, manifest or convention descriptors before materialization.
boundary: Fixed-width integers stay fixed; overflow near 32- and 64-bit indexing maxima; rebuild old inputs without old-format support.
oracle: Independent target-layout oracle and loader outcome; no frozen historical numeric-ID or decoder compatibility assertion.

positive: Build no-std/no-implicit-prelude programs with explicitly supplied core/allocator/runtime dependencies as needed.
negative: Reject absent required dependencies and a name-copied counterfeit intrinsic despite disabling the prelude.
boundary: Core-only versus allocation-enabled dependency closure and explicit imports shadowing prelude candidates.
oracle: Selected dependency/manifest closure and public names are inspected; no ambient filesystem or host grants.

positive: A finite proof succeeds with adequate advertised budget and repeats deterministically.
negative: Exhaust trait, alias, const, row, layout and lifetime proof budgets; require explicit resource outcomes and no guessed evidence/artifact.
boundary: One-below/exact/one-above limits, cyclic user traits and malformed inputs under low budgets.
oracle: Resource diagnostic category, bounded work counters and no publication; limit failure is not a successful semantic rejection witness.

positive: Handle a lawful terminal source effect and resume ordinary execution; return a recoverable host Result error.
negative: Abort, primitive/host/internal faults and supervision termination must not masquerade as recoverable source failure or successful cleanup.
boundary: Run each terminal category in isolation with event capture; test optional cancellation separately.
oracle: Distinct outcome category plus specified cleanup prefix; fatal faults do not execute ordinary Drop cleanup.

positive: Run scalar, effect-order and deterministic-format fixtures against independent mathematical/golden oracles on both engines.
negative: Detect implicit fast-math, debug-only overflow, locale-dependent output and NaN/signed-zero policy drift.
boundary: Subnormals, midpoint rounding, infinities, MIN division, optimization and target-width changes.
oracle: Exact bits/bytes and effect/drop trace; VM/native agreement alone is not an oracle because both may share a bug.

positive: Normalize Bool and Option to the same concrete Result layouts and trait instances.
negative: Reject overlapping alias-specific impls or differing behavior based only on written alias spelling.
boundary: Nested generic aliases, references and public re-exports.
oracle: Selected type/trait identity and structural value equality.

positive: Use true and Some(()) interchangeably at Bool type with no cast.
negative: Reject implicit coercion to Result<(),UnrelatedError>.
boundary: Pattern matching and generic expected-type selection preserve the monomorphic Bool error type.
oracle: Type equality and chosen variant; no truthiness conversion path.

positive: Materialize None<T> separately for scalar and exact-linear payload instantiations and match it structurally.
negative: Reject treating None as an unrestricted memoized generic owner or invoking runtime initialization from a constant pattern.
boundary: Nested arrays/tuples and imported constant aliases with binder shadowing.
oracle: Structural constant scheme, per-occurrence type and zero runtime initializer calls.

positive: Default Bool to false and Option<NoDefault> to None.
negative: Reject overlapping blanket Result Default or an alias-specific duplicate.
boundary: Generic defaults must not require the absent Option payload to implement Default.
oracle: Variant result and coherence outcome independently checked.

positive: Result::as_refs retains a borrowed error; Option::as_ref produces a unit error, with shared/mutable counterparts.
negative: Reject substituting Result<&T,&()> for Option<&T> or extending a projected reference beyond its owner.
boundary: Both variants and repeated reborrows with mutation visible in the original resident.
oracle: Exact output types, loan origins and address identity.

positive: Replace and swap unique exact-linear residents; return the old resident and explicitly complete each owner.
negative: Reject any implementation/client path that duplicates or discards the old value, or requires Clone/affine bounds.
boundary: Self-alias prevention, zero-sized residents and take evaluating Default before a hole opens.
oracle: Resident IDs and event order show no destructor or Clone during replacement/swap.

positive: Discard affine values and legally empty availability while preserving cleanup.
negative: Reject discard of exact-linear values and exact-positive continuations, including through generic helper wrappers.
boundary: Zero-sized and nested resident obligations cannot disappear through unit-like representation.
oracle: Source ownership diagnostic and no artifact; destruction never counts as a required use.

positive: Complete if/else consumes one shared ticket in either selected inline branch.
negative: Reject duplicated consumption in one branch or two separately formed owning closures capturing it.
boundary: Both branch outcomes, aliases and nested conditionals with observable capture construction.
oracle: Exactly one selected body and one disposition of each resident.

positive: An uncovered conditional is legal only if its skipped environment is lawfully discardable or subsequently sealed inline.
negative: Reject a normally completing skipped branch that strands a linear capture.
boundary: Constant conditions are not used to hide the nonconstant case; include bottom selected alternatives.
oracle: Per-path owner obligation diagnostic, not an unconditional affine bound that rejects valid covered alternatives.

positive: Store a fully sealed Result after compatible normal post-states join.
negative: Reject saving an unsealed if result in locals, fields, returns or opaque generic calls.
boundary: Moving or aliasing that Result cannot let a later else retroactively repair the original boundary.
oracle: Guard provenance remains tied to the originating result; diagnostic locates the escape.

positive: Recovery after a selected callback returns Err observes the callback's mutations and transferred ownership.
negative: Reject a recovery callback that assumes the untouched incoming environment.
boundary: Compare left-failed-without-callback and callback-produced-failure paths in one chain.
oracle: Callback/effect sequence and guarded post-state, including failure payload ownership.

positive: Enumerate and/or truth paths including both callbacks executing in sequence.
negative: Reject a second invocation requiring a consumed capture or falsely treating sequential alternatives as exclusive.
boundary: Repeated nested chains with distinct effect rows and changing environment states.
oracle: Path table counts 0/1/2 callbacks and validates each applicable RunsIn transition.

positive: Allow a linear payload on the preserved side and affine payload on the discarded side of each operator.
negative: Reject exact-linear success discard in if/and and exact-linear error discard in else/or.
boundary: Not swaps both sides with no discard bound; refined pack disposal is checked separately.
oracle: Compile-positive/negative matrix changes only the relevant payload principal class.

positive: Compose callbacks/iterators/readers/writers with disjoint rows and declare their normalized union.
negative: Reject omitted outward effects, ambiguous row splits and forged pure callback summaries.
boundary: Associated row projections and duplicate same-family instances distinguished by generic arguments.
oracle: Selected exact effect row and observable effect calls; no forcing unrelated rows equal.

positive: Skip an affine materialized callback and clean its captures without invocation.
negative: Reject skipping an independently owned callback containing a linear resident.
boundary: A correlated inline alternative is not subjected to the same unconditional discard bound.
oracle: Capture ledger and invocation count distinguish physical owning values from shared contextual evidence.

positive: Expose a pattern binder only through the justified positive or negative hidden binding argument.
negative: Reject binder escape, wrong-polarity use and a custom If impl that claims forged lexical authority.
boundary: Empty versus nonempty Args/BorrowArgs, shadowed names and borrowed noncopy projections.
oracle: Sealed binder keys, actual Fn argument tuple and original loan provenance.

positive: Exercise all four Result/BranchResult carrier pairs for and/or with correct merge and common-context projection.
negative: Reject exporting a name present on only one success alternative or merging equal-spelled distinct binders.
boundary: Borrow inherited packs on the right, introduce fresh binders, and close only lawfully discardable excluded residents.
oracle: Context algebra P+Q and intersections checked against origin identities and owner/loan ledger, not spelling.

positive: Apply not twice to a refined carrier and recover original payloads, contexts and loans.
negative: Reject a fabricated Not implementation/evidence path that loses guards or substitutes a plain Result for a context carrier.
boundary: Both polarities, empty contexts and observable resident pack cleanup.
oracle: Involution on valid payload/context identities with no duplication or erasure of residents.

positive: Rename every control function and directly imported operation through explicit and re-export aliases.
negative: An unrelated same-spelled binding must not gain call, binder, label or loop privileges.
boundary: Qualified calls, word fixity aliases and no-implicit-prelude variants.
oracle: Same semantic trace and ownership acceptance modulo declaration renaming; no wrappers inserted solely for forwarding.

positive: Pass a stored or inline exhaustive pattern callable to ordinary match with exact Fn<(T,)> evidence.
negative: Reject nonexhaustive input, mismatched argument pack or effect-operation arms used as first-class handler values.
boundary: Multi-argument versus one-tuple input, ordered clauses and shared captures.
oracle: One callable invocation transferring subject exactly once; clause event and result contract.

positive: Borrow-match an opaque linear subject or transfer it through every authorized owned clause.
negative: Reject wildcard/rest disposal of an owned linear subject even when it makes the patterns exhaustive.
boundary: Linear fields under affine-looking enum shells and zero-sized tickets.
oracle: Separate exhaustiveness success from ownership failure using valid syntax and resolved types.

positive: Use return, try and break_at through generic helpers to the supplied active label, protecting the payload before cleanup.
negative: Reject mismatched label result types, escape and an opaque helper boundary without direct-control proof.
boundary: Try Ok returns locally; Err leaves; error factories run only on their selected paths.
oracle: Direct destination and exact payload/cleanup trace at O0 and optimized execution.

positive: Compare normal loop fallthrough with matching continue using the same state transition and cleanup events.
negative: Reject a library backedge that retains an iteration delimiter or silently lowers a required tail edge as an ordinary call.
boundary: Loop_at and loop_state, repeated reborrows and per-iteration owners.
oracle: Checked backedge proof plus equal state/output and bounded live-control metrics.

positive: Accept a loop whose temporary loans and cleanup end before the checked backedge.
negative: Reject dead-local argument borrows, live completion transformations, retained capture state and incompatible ABI tail transfer.
boundary: Run every source diagnostic at O0 and all shipped optimized levels.
oracle: Failure is a source proof diagnostic, not optimization-dependent acceptance or runtime stack overflow.

positive: Nest loops with the same break result type; each break reaches its own fresh brand.
negative: Reject substituting an outer label brand or an unbranded LoopControl<B> contract for the generative family.
boundary: Recursive loop factories and a body that names its proof-only L argument.
oracle: Exact effect-instance IDs and loop event trace; equal payload types do not merge handlers.

positive: Infer an inner loop's break only from its nearest explicit contextual LoopControl instance.
negative: Reject an inner payload type mismatch even when an outer loop would accept that payload.
boundary: Forwarded tails and union reordering cannot become alternate default-instance search paths.
oracle: Diagnostic refers to the inner expected instance; no outer catch event or artifact.

positive: continue_at selects its explicit label-indexed handler; break_at exits the label scope rather than restarting it.
negative: Reject continue_at with no matching active loop handler, despite valid Label evidence.
boundary: Nested loop_at calls sharing one L use nearest exact handler; distinct labels explicitly reach outer loops.
oracle: Destination/handler events distinguish local break return, label exit and iteration restart.

positive: Restore a moved-out unique referent before break or continue that ends its loan.
negative: Reject a hole crossing cleanup-bearing loop exit or captured continuation even though the operation returns bottom.
boundary: Outer captured owner versus explicit loop-state transfer and nested reborrow cases.
oracle: Initialization proof and source diagnostic identify the invalid loan boundary.

positive: Move exact-linear S through Continue and return exact-linear B through Break, explicitly completing the final B.
negative: Reject duplicate/drop of either branch payload or a backedge lacking replacement S.
boundary: Zero iterations where an API allows them, multiple transitions, noncopy nested state and zero-sized residents.
oracle: Per-transition ownership conservation; no Clone, implicit disposal or hidden resident copy.

positive: Run loop/loop_at/loop_state for geometric counts after warmup with handler and capture instrumentation.
negative: A retained-handler-chain mutation must fail the same measurement without relying on eventual stack overflow.
boundary: Nested loops, normal/explicit continue and user callbacks with drops.
oracle: Maximum live frames, delimiters and retained continuation bytes remain independent of iteration count.

positive: Expand every integer operation over all twelve widths and compare ordinary/checked/wrapping/saturating/overflowing policies.
negative: Trap or return None for each specified invalid case; never invoke a trapping leaf to implement checked failure.
boundary: MIN/MAX, zero, MIN/-1, unsigned negation, count N-1/N/N+1, radix 1/2/36/37, signed shifts and Euclidean signs.
oracle: Independent arbitrary-precision integer model with explicit target width and precise parse error offsets.

positive: Expand all 196 source/destination scalar pairs for As, TryAs and ExactAs, with exact selected output/error types.
negative: Reject unrepresentable checked/exact inputs and forbidden char/reference/Bool coercions without trying a multi-step conversion chain.
boundary: Negative fractions to unsigned, half-open MAX+1, NaNs/infinities/zeros and integer-to-float midpoint/precision boundaries.
oracle: Exact integer/rational and destination-rounding oracle; test all 588 policy/pair cells, not a host cast reused as truth.

positive: Canonicalize all tested NaN bit classes and implement IEEE PartialEq/PartialOrd with no float Eq/Ord/Hash instances.
negative: Reject float total-order/hash-key trait requirements and detect ordinary comparisons that make NaN reflexive or signed zeros unequal.
boundary: Positive/negative quiet/signaling NaNs, infinities, subnormals and adjacent floats for both widths.
oracle: Exact canonical bits, IEEE equality and unordered comparison results, and absence of implicit total/hash-key evidence.

positive: Compare named IEEE operations with ordinary PartialEq/PartialOrd and the explicitly named total_cmp on NaNs and signed zeros.
negative: Detect an ordered operator returning true for NaN or a partial comparison inconsistent with IEEE equality.
boundary: Every pair of float classes and both scalar widths.
oracle: Ordinary and named IEEE operations agree; explicit total_cmp distinguishes signed zeros and orders canonical NaN with exact Ordering/Option values.

positive: Parse exact decimal halfway/near-halfway values directly to f32/f64 using ties-to-even.
negative: Reject malformed exponent, separator, trailing input and finite overflow with byte-oriented diagnostics/errors.
boundary: Double-rounding counterexamples, minimum subnormal, underflow, largest finite, special spellings and signed zero.
oracle: Independent exact decimal rational to binary-rounding oracle plus golden shortest/exact formatting vectors.

positive: Validate and decode Unicode scalar boundary vectors; encode writes only the required prefix.
negative: Reject invalid lead/continuation, overlong, surrogate, out-of-range and every truncation position without a VM trap.
boundary: Empty input, valid prefix followed by invalid sequence, all scalar ranges and sentinel bytes after output.
oracle: First malformed lead offset, kind and optional error length; independent UTF-8 model and exact output bytes.

positive: Slice/split/remove text at valid byte/scalar boundaries and return views into original storage.
negative: For multiply invalid ranges return Reversed before OutOfBounds before NotCharBoundary, without mutation.
boundary: Empty, end-of-buffer, multi-byte scalars, reversed out-of-range requests and allocation-failing edits.
oracle: Byte-range model, exact error variant and unchanged original UTF-8 contents.

positive: from_utf8_recover returns the original Vec bytes and ownership on invalid input; success transfers storage to String.
negative: Detect losing, replacing or duplicating the failed input buffer; no fault-based recovery.
boundary: Every malformed class, empty buffer, reserved spare capacity and zero-length success.
oracle: Resident/allocation identity and returned bytes; distinguish the explicitly discarding shorter from_utf8 API.

positive: Read String/Vec/Slice views while their original owner and loan remain valid; mutate after last use.
negative: Reject reallocation, owner move/destruction or incompatible mutation while a borrowed view is still live.
boundary: Views stored in aggregates/iterators and returned via a helper keep original input lifetime relations.

negative: Reject missing public declarations, placeholder bodies, wrong namespaces, duplicate effect wrappers and whole-library algorithms substituted by host primitives.
boundary: Build each dependency profile with/without automatic prelude, rename imports and materialize otherwise unreachable generic methods and selected trait instances.
oracle: Public-interface and body-reachability ledger ties each specified declaration/family expansion to actual source and executed client roots; compilation alone does not prove behavior.

positive: For every public operation, compile its exact signature and a legal client; execute success/completion with each admitted ownership class and valid non-static borrows.
negative: Delete or weaken each relevant bound/lifetime/row in an adversarial client/implementation pair and require rejection; recoverable failure cannot lose incoming owners.
boundary: All return/error variants, skipped callbacks, validation-before-mutation, partial initialization and explicitly promised complexity.
oracle: Per-declaration contract checklist records input/output ownership, receiver lifetime, callback trace and completion; no unexecuted generic body counts as covered.

positive: Exercise fundamental PartialEq/Eq/PartialOrd/Ord/Hash/Clone/Default/Display/Debug/As traits on all required concrete and structural families.
negative: Reject overlapping impls and insufficient declared bounds; partial comparison alone grants neither total-order nor hash-key evidence; lawful safe traits are not unsafe layout or size proofs.
boundary: Alias coherence, reference versus referent cloning, generic outcomes with nonprintable linear residents and missing optional instances.
oracle: Per-cell trait resolution plus partial/total comparison, hash and clone laws; explicit exclusions such as float Eq/Ord/Hash are rejected, while a dash merely means not required.

positive: Select every independent arithmetic/bit/comparison trait and canonical prefix/infix binding with its exact signature and empty row.
negative: Reject missing operator impl, implicit borrowing/promotion, conflicting fixity and noncopy owned comparison without its affine bound.
boundary: All listed precedences and associativities, custom operators on owners/references and separate neg/sub identities.
oracle: Grouping and trait-resolution oracle plus one-evaluation operand trace; no giant privileged Arithmetic trait.

positive: Run all Result/Option algebra, projection, slot and zip/unzip/flatten/transpose operations through every structural variant.
negative: Reject missing payload discard/Clone/duplication bounds and detect lost inputs on zip failures or slot replacement.
boundary: Factories/observers run only on specified branches; Bool parse accepts exactly true/false and from_u8 only 0/1.
oracle: Explicit variant equations, borrowed origins, callback counts and input-owner conservation; Some(false) is successful parsing.

positive: Check half-open range operations, left-biased extrema, Ordering then/then_with and private NonZero for every integer width.
negative: Reject reversed/bounds/overflow cases in specified precedence, invalid clamp bounds and zero NonZero construction.
boundary: Touching/empty/reversed ranges, relative offsets near signed limits and min/max ties with distinct identities.
oracle: Independent integer interval model and preserved error inputs; NonZero construction cannot be bypassed by wrapping casts.

positive: Cover scalar family methods omitted from short checklist names: bit counts/rotations/bytes/logs, float classification/rounding/next values/FMA and approximate comparison.
negative: Reject invalid radix/tolerance; exact intermediate overflow must not make approximate comparison spuriously true.
boundary: Signed Euclidean arithmetic, zero bit counts, no-promotion, FMA single-rounding cases and shortest-format tie-breaking.
oracle: Independent integer/exact-rational/rounding models and exact text vectors with named special-value policies.

positive: Exercise every ASCII predicate/case/digit/escape method and text iterator/search/split/line/edit operation.
negative: Reject invalid radix/scalar/index/edit requests before mutation and preserve contents on allocation failure.
boundary: Empty separators/searches, LF/CRLF/lone CR, terminal newline, non-ASCII unchanged case and malformed-subsequence lossy decoding.
oracle: Independent byte/scalar and iterator reference model; implementation must document the fixed lossy-subsequence policy before its oracle is approved.

positive: Exercise all fixed-array and Slice/SliceMut methods including swaps/rotations/copy/clone/fill and array conversion/creation.
negative: Reject mismatched length/bounds/ownership classes; partial array initialization on nonlocal exit cannot discard linear outputs.
boundary: Every construction index, empty/ZST arrays, trapping index versus checked get and shared/unique reborrow lifetimes.
oracle: Sequence/ownership model and increasing-index callback trace; failure returns full source for checked array conversion.

positive: Cover every Vec/Deque/Heap method, aliases Stack/WorkList, sequence conversions and borrowed-view operation.
negative: Reject invalid indexes/rotations and unsafe mutable heap-key access; detect owner loss on replacing an equal/maximum resident.
boundary: Deque wraparound/as_slices, amortized endpoint work at geometric sizes, max-heap ties and ascending into_sorted_vec.
oracle: Independent sequence/heap model with exact promised order and logical complexity counters; growth factor/backing representation are not frozen.

positive: Cover every map/set/entry/query/iteration/set-algebra operation with colliding lawful keys and a mutable value payload.
negative: Reject missing Eq/Hash/Equivalent bounds and key mutation while resident; bad safe trait laws must not cause memory unsafety.
boundary: Occupied/vacant callbacks, duplicate representative policy, disjoint mutable-value iteration and all set relations.
oracle: Reference map/set contents, returned resident identities and loan ledger; compare unordered results as sets unless a stronger order is specified.

positive: Instantiate all iterator/adapter/consumer families with exact Item, Effects and completion/marker contracts.
negative: Reject unjustified ExactSize/DoubleEnded/Fused claims, unsafe reliance on a lying size_hint and borrowed callback lifetime extension.
boundary: Non-fused Some-after-None sources, zero/exact take/skip counts, interleaved ends, enumerate overflow and all into_parts buffers.
oracle: Independent pull-event/state model; adapter creation has no polling effects and full source/callback row unions survive export.

positive: Expand every predicate and fallible predicate family and test search, bounds, dedup and ordered traversal methods.
negative: Detect callbacks after short-circuit/first Err, returned references to temporaries or destruction of lossless partial output.
boundary: Empty all=true/any=false, second match for find_unique, reverse visitation, duplicate search keys and empty needle.
oracle: Declared traversal/stopping rules and exact borrowed origins; binary_search may return any equal index, unlike lower_bound.

positive: Exercise every digest/formatter/diagnostic constructor and accessor with exact scalar, quoted, indentation and fingerprint bytes.
negative: Reject invalid hex lengths/digits and bounded-output violations; preserve a rejected diagnostic with all structured fields.
boundary: Digest upper/lower hex policy only when specified, nested formatting, blank lines and unknown source locations.
oracle: Pinned bytes/structured fields; unspecified presentation choices require a documented versioned policy rather than invented canonical expectations.

positive: Instantiate every layout/raw-pointer/Box/C-string operation for representative alignment, ownership and target types.
negative: Safe signature tests reject missing unsafe scopes and wrong ownership bounds; isolated invalid raw contracts exercise available instrumentation.
boundary: All pointer cast/offset/unaligned/overlap forms, allocator provenance, PhantomData not establishing lifetime and C scalar aliases.
oracle: Explicit safe/unsafe obligation ledger, target layout model and matching completion domains; no UB execution in normal test workers.

positive: Exercise all endian reader/writer/patch operations, marks, alignment, resize, hex and optional Base64 profiles.
negative: Reject malformed padding/tails/digits, wrong marks, invalid alignment and arithmetic overflow without partial mutation.
boundary: Every fixed-width truncation, all six Base64 alphabet/padding combinations and canonical empty/one/two/three-byte tails.
oracle: Independent codec bytes and exact error positions; optional modules report explicit profile coverage rather than fake success.

positive: Run IndexVec/Arena/GenArena/Interner/StringInterner/BitSet/SparseSet/WorkQueue/UndoLog public operations against small reference models.
negative: Reject wrong tag types, invalid marks/generations/index overflow and duplicate linear-value loss.
boundary: BitSet sorted output, SparseSet unspecified order, FIFO pending dedup/requeue, nested undo marks and empty transfer completion.
oracle: Content/order/owner state machines and checked representability; no hidden compiler-specific semantic callback is needed in the library.

positive: Exercise every source/budget/parser/graph helper with deterministic fake inputs and explicit remaining work/ownership.
negative: Detect hidden file reads/timers, rollback of unrelated effects, missing input-sized charges and incorrect rejected-ticket ownership.
boundary: Zero/exact/overflow limits, invalid source coordinates, cyclic graphs and nested state marks.
oracle: Independent model plus instrumented logical operations; advertised charge schedule must be specified rather than inferred from wall time.

positive: Exercise every host operation/stream trait through fake providers and a substantive run_compiler_host handler with exact authority.
negative: Reject wrong host bindings and unauthorized families; partial I/O/unsupported atomic replacement must be typed outcomes, not fatal wrapper traps.
boundary: Atomic replace all-or-nothing where advertised versus Unsupported, binary/diagnostic separation and MemoryCursor read/write/seek.
oracle: Provider call/result ledger and committed-prefix model; no real filesystem/process side effects are necessary for these contract tests.

positive: Cover every path/file/process/time/random operation with target-vector fixtures and scriptable providers.
negative: Reject missing grants, invalid duration/range, bad encoding and protocol completion that loses a live owner or produced result.
boundary: Platform prefixes, close/wait variants, directory-order permutations, terminated-but-unreaped child and complete random-fill failure.
oracle: Target-specific value models and deterministic event schedules; no implicit filesystem containment, cryptographic, durability or timing promises.

positive: Implement minimal source test Generator/Future/task providers and exercise every protocol declaration without selecting a production executor.
negative: Reject lost Pending/worker/result owners, label/context lifetime escapes, generic linear cancellation and phantom output from await.
boundary: All bounded wake/cancel/complete/provider-close interleavings and nested deep-handler effects under non-static captures.
oracle: Explicit provider state machine and per-owner/resumption ledger; no async keyword, implicit threads or scheduler fairness assumption.

positive: Instantiate each required trait-table cell and each error constructor/variant; prove every opaque owner has a lawful public completion path.
negative: Reject missing required instances, alias overlaps, fabricated default IDs and lost linear generic error payloads; do not invent negative impls for dashes.
boundary: All advertised tuple arities, zero/one/nonzero arrays, leaf-error Debug/Display and nonprintable generic recovered owners.
oracle: Cell-by-cell surface/behavior ledger and exact error-kind/offset/precedence; no forced Error trait merely from a type name.

positive: Invoke catch_fail once and translate a lawful terminal Fail into Err; Report resumes once and preserves normal execution.
negative: Reject catching Fail by abandoning must-move residents, using abort as recoverable failure or resuming Report zero/two times.
boundary: Assertions/expect/unreachable terminate through defined abort, with no optimizer assumption or guaranteed diagnostic output; error payloads remain protected.
oracle: Distinct outcome and cleanup traces, exact callback/resumption counts and compatible handler post-environments.

positive: repeat_n calls once per increasing index; while_do checks condition before each body and unions their distinct effect rows.
negative: Reject a repeated callback that consumes unreplaced captured state or a precomputed Bool passed as a callable condition.
boundary: Zero count, initially false condition, nonlocal exit in condition/body and overflow-sensitive index limits.
oracle: Exact call/event sequence and actual reusable Fn/RunsIn evidence; neither helper invents an implicit break protocol.
